awd_titl_txt: CC* Strategy-Campus: Accelerating Research Computing at Texas A&M San Antonio (ARCATS)
awd_abstract_narration:
Accelerating Research Computing at Texas A&M University-San Antonio (ARCATS) elevates research computing capacity by enhancing the capacity for campus cyberinfrastructure-enabled research. The university has recognized the growing importance of data-intensive computational science across a wide range of academic fields, including water resources management, genomics, biology, chemistry, health, humanities, and cybersecurity.   Supporting the university’s growing research programs, ARCATS develops a comprehensive plan to advance the university’s cyberinfrastructure and facilitate collaborations with regional cyberinfrastructure partners. Through this process, ARCATS is identifying specific research needs in high performance computing, plans for research computing resources, and mechanisms that support burgeoning research communities of practice. 

The project supports undergraduate and graduate education through experiential learning opportunities, fostering computation-related science programs, and developing student-focused industry partnerships.  ARCATS positions the university in the national cyberinfrastructure ecosystem by promoting research and instruction-focused collaborations with institutions in Texas and national research communities. As such, it serves as a model for smaller institutions, fostering regional and national scientific collaborations.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

Project Outcomes Report

CC* Strategy-Campus: Accelerating Research Computing at Texas A&M University–San Antonio (ARCATS)

NSF Award No.: 2430335
Institution: Texas A&M University–San Antonio
Principal Investigator: Dr. Izzat Alsmadi

The Accelerating Research Computing at Texas A&M University–San Antonio (ARCATS) project strengthened the university’s ability to support research that depends on advanced computing, large datasets, and artificial intelligence. The project focused on identifying campus research-computing needs, developing a strategic plan for cyberinfrastructure, expanding access to high-performance computing resources, and connecting faculty and students with regional and national research-computing partners. It established a foundation for broader participation in computational research at a Hispanic-Serving Institution in South Texas.

ARCATS supported two major campus workshops in 2025. The April workshop provided hands-on exposure to high-performance computing, access to the Texas A&M University computing environment, JupyterLab, Python, artificial intelligence, machine learning, and deep learning. The September workshop brought together university researchers, computing professionals, and external experts to discuss research needs, infrastructure priorities, sustainability, and a campus research-computing roadmap. Project records report more than 45 workshop participants. They also indicate that more than 20 students continued using high-performance computing resources independently and that three faculty members initiated computing-based proposals or pilot studies. These numerical outcomes should be confirmed against institutional records before submission.

A major outcome was a campus cyberinfrastructure assessment and strategic roadmap addressing computing resources, data storage, networking, security, governance, staffing, training, and long-term sustainability. The work strengthened research-computing support and user onboarding and helped position the university’s CAMSA computing resources and partnerships to support interdisciplinary work. The resulting capacity benefits research and education in areas such as biology, genomics, chemistry, health sciences, humanities, cybersecurity, and data-intensive computing. ARCATS provides a foundation for continued investment, external funding, student experiential learning, and collaboration with the broader research-computing community.
